bulk.blockAmnesty.blurb: Clear your block list completely and start over.
bulk.blockAmnesty.effect1: Every account on your block list is unblocked.
bulk.blockAmnesty.effect2: They can follow you, see your posts and interact with you again.
bulk.blockAmnesty.effect3: They are not notified that you blocked them, or that you stopped.
bulk.blockAmnesty.effect4: This can only be undone if you backed up your block list first.
bulk.blockAmnesty.label: Block amnesty — unblock everyone
bulk.blockAmnesty.title: Unblock every account you have blocked?
bulk.checkFailed: Couldn’t check what this would do: {{error}}
bulk.listFollow.blurb: Follow every account in one of your lists that you are not following yet.
bulk.listFollow.effect1: Every member of the list you are not already following gets followed.
bulk.listFollow.effect2: Accounts that require approval get a follow request instead, which they can decline.
bulk.listFollow.effect3: Their posts start appearing in your home timeline as well as the list.
bulk.listFollow.effect4: Accounts you already follow are left exactly as they are.
bulk.listFollow.label: Follow everyone on a list
bulk.listFollow.title: Follow everyone on this {{source}}?
bulk.listUnfollow.blurb: Stop following every account in one of your lists.
bulk.listUnfollow.effect1: Every member of the list you currently follow gets unfollowed.
bulk.listUnfollow.effect2: Any pending follow requests to members are withdrawn.
bulk.listUnfollow.effect3: Most servers only keep accounts you follow in a list, so the list may end up empty. The list itself is never deleted.
bulk.listUnfollow.effect4: Nobody is blocked or muted, and nobody is told.
bulk.listUnfollow.label: Unfollow everyone on a list
bulk.listUnfollow.title: Unfollow everyone on this {{source}}?
bulk.muteAmnesty.blurb: Clear your mute list completely and start over.
bulk.muteAmnesty.effect1: Every account on your mute list is unmuted.
bulk.muteAmnesty.effect2: Their posts and notifications start reaching you again.
bulk.muteAmnesty.effect3: Muted words and filters are not affected — this is only accounts.
bulk.muteAmnesty.effect4: This can only be undone if you backed up your mute list first.
bulk.muteAmnesty.label: Mute amnesty — unmute everyone
bulk.muteAmnesty.title: Unmute every account you have muted?
bulk.plan.counting: Checking how many accounts this affects…
bulk.reblogsOff.blurb: Keep following everyone, but stop their boosts from reaching your home timeline.
bulk.reblogsOff.effect1: You keep following everyone — nobody is unfollowed.
bulk.reblogsOff.effect2: Their own posts still appear in your home timeline.
bulk.reblogsOff.effect3: Boosts they make stop appearing there.
bulk.reblogsOff.effect4: You can turn retweets back on for everyone, or per account on their profile.
bulk.reblogsOff.label: Turn off retweets for all friends
bulk.reblogsOff.title: Turn off retweets for everyone you follow?
bulk.reblogsOn.blurb: Let boosts from everyone you follow back into your home timeline.
bulk.reblogsOn.effect1: Boosts from everyone you follow start appearing in your home timeline again.
bulk.reblogsOn.effect2: This includes accounts you had individually silenced boosts for.
bulk.reblogsOn.effect3: Nothing else about who you follow changes.
bulk.reblogsOn.label: Turn on retweets for all friends
bulk.reblogsOn.title: Turn on retweets for everyone you follow?
bulk.stopped: Stopped counting. Nothing has been changed.
bulk.stopped.hint: No accounts were touched — this only ever read your list. Count again to see what this action would do.

bulk.summary.unfollow.allOther: This will unfollow all {{about}}{{count}} members of this {{source}}.

settings.accounts.footnote.before: Deleting data removes this browser's saved settings for that account — RSS feeds, linked accounts, local moderation and similar. It never touches anything on the server. For a key-by-key view of the current account, see
settings.accounts.intro: Every credential saved in this browser, and the local data each one owns. Use this to clean up duplicate logins, or to reset one account's local data without signing out of it.
settings.accounts.title: Signed-in accounts
settings.anonymous.intro: Control how the browser-local Anonymous home feed is assembled.
settings.anonymous.maxAge: Maximum age of posts from followed accounts
settings.anonymous.maxAge.hint: Older posts are left out when Anonymous builds Home. Posts from followed hashtags are not affected.
settings.anonymous.title: Anonymous
settings.appearance.expandSpoilers: Always expand posts marked with content warnings
settings.appearance.intro: Adjust how the web interface looks and behaves.
settings.appearance.title: Appearance
settings.blue.ai.hint: Hides Eliza, the OpenRouter chat, AI translation and the search and hashtag suggestions. Nothing is deleted — your OpenRouter key and your conversations stay where they are, and turning this back on restores them.
settings.blue.analytics.hint: Anonymous page counts only — which kinds of page get used, never which account, post or tag you looked at, and never a query string. Turn this off and the analytics script is never loaded at all: nothing is fetched, counted or sent. The script is served from this site, not from a third party.
settings.blue.art.hint: Which bird and which fail whale the app draws. The hand-drawn set is the default — they were drawn for this app, by hand, on paper. The generated ones are the originals, kept for anyone who prefers them.
settings.blue.autoRefresh: Auto-refresh timeline — new posts arrive continually, without you asking
settings.blue.autoRefresh.hint: Off by default, and worth leaving off: a feed that rewrites itself moves the post you were halfway through reading. Mastodon only — Twitter, Bluesky and RSS are polled and are not affected.
settings.blue.checks.everyone: Everyone, because everyone deserves a blue check mark
settings.blue.checks.relative: More followers than me — compared to me, they're famous
settings.blue.checks.top: Top accounts only (a fixed follower bar)
settings.blue.confirmPost: Ask "do you really want to post that?" before posting
settings.blue.custom.hint: Overrides ride on top of the theme; reset any of them to fall back to the theme's own color. A custom link color replaces the accent preset above.
settings.blue.delayedSend: Wait 30 seconds before posting, so you can cancel (or publish early)
settings.blue.feedReader: Reader mode for feeds (reader typography, no pictures)
settings.blue.ignoreCooldown.hint: Keeps “Load more” working past the maximum, with no cooldown. The break is a health guard, not a technical limit — this is here because it is your call, and it lives in Settings rather than at the end of the feed so that turning it off is a decision rather than a reflex.
settings.blue.maxPosts.hint: “You’ve had enough for now.” Load more is disabled once the feed reaches this size; it lifts after about an hour or when you reload.
settings.blue.minPosts.hint: Auto-loads more until the feed holds at least this many posts (or the timeline runs out).
settings.blue.miniComposer: Open the mini composer on Home automatically
settings.blue.miniComposer.hint: Off by default: Home offers Write and Quick post, and the small box appears when you ask for it. Turn this on to have it open on arrival. Thoughtful posting, above, overrides this. These also live on
settings.blue.showImages: Show images in feeds (off replaces pictures with a 🖼️ chip)
settings.blue.theme.hint: Automatic follows your system preference. Everything on this page applies immediately and saved in this browser.
settings.blue.thoughtful.hint: Home drops the Quick post button, leaving only Write, and that editor only saves. You post later, from Drafts. Replies, chats and paste shares are never held back — they're urgent, or already deliberate.
settings.blue.typography.hint: Applies to reader mode on threads and, when feed reader is on, to every timeline.
settings.blue.zen.label: Hide both sidebars — just you and the feed
settings.bulk.footnote: Every one of these asks for confirmation first, and tells you exactly how many accounts it would touch before you agree to it.
settings.bulk.groupAccounts: Everyone you follow, mute or block
settings.bulk.intro: Changes applied to everyone at once. Mastodon has no bulk API for any of these, so each one is applied account by account — a big list takes a while, and the server may pause us along the way. You can leave this page while a job runs; it keeps going.
settings.bulk.noLists: You have no lists yet. Make one from the Feeds menu and these actions will apply to it.
settings.bulk.title: Bulk moderation
settings.config.conflict: Your settings changed on another device, and this browser also has unsaved changes.
settings.config.export.hint: Every export is checked at runtime against the storage registry and the credentials currently stored in this browser. Pastepile publishing is anonymous and deliberately omits your Pastepile API key so its permanent-paste option remains available.
settings.config.includePrivate.hint: Adds your home server, custom CORS proxy address, and branded link-shortener setup. Never includes credentials, account-scoped settings, follows, blocks or mutes, RSS or paste feeds, lists, bookmarks, saved searches, local moderation, activity history, drafts, or authored content.
settings.config.intro: Move browser settings between devices or keep them synced from a URL.
settings.config.key.clientPrefs: Appearance, reading, composing, and accessibility preferences
settings.config.key.translationUsage: Translation usage counters (counts only — never translated text)
settings.config.publish.hint: This creates a permanent, unlisted Pastepile. Its edit password will be kept only in this browser and the paste will appear under My Pastes for later editing or deletion.
settings.config.readOnly: Settings are no longer being saved to your account, because storing them there is part of Mawkingbird Plus. Everything already stored stays readable and can be exported at any time.
settings.config.remote.hint: Automatic checks compare the remote file's SHA-256 hash and ignore local UI changes. A changed remote file prompts before import. Every remote response is immediately fetched again; a source that cannot return the same hash twice is limited to on-demand checks.
settings.config.sync.offSince: Not syncing on this browser — last saved {{when}}.
settings.config.sync.offer: Keep these settings on your Mawkingbird account so they follow you to your other browsers.
settings.config.sync.offer.hint.after: settings and makes them your profile. Your other browsers will take these settings the next time you use them, so it's worth a look first if this isn't the browser you set up on.
settings.config.sync.remoteExists: Your account has settings synced from another browser.
settings.config.sync.resume.hint: Your account's settings are taken first, so this browser matches your others. If this browser has changes your account doesn't, you'll be asked which to keep.
settings.config.sync.stop.hint: Stopping keeps everything as it is — nothing is deleted, and you can turn it back on.
settings.config.title: Import/Export Config
settings.content.everyone.hint: Applies to every post from every account, on this Mastodon account only. Stored in this browser — it is a reading preference, not something the server knows about.
settings.content.expandCw.note: Posts with a content warning render already open. The warning text is still shown above the post, so you always know one was set.
settings.content.flipside.after: : that page is for accounts you want less of, this one is for accounts you want without a doorway in front of them.
settings.content.footnote: Trust never overrides a filter. A word filter you set, or a post your server chose to hide, stays hidden — those are your rules and the server's, and one person being trusted is not a reason to break them.
settings.content.howFar.hint: One choice, so there is never a question of which setting wins. Whoever this covers, their content warnings open on their own and their sensitive media renders unblurred.
settings.content.independent: The switches above are what Mawkingbird itself obeys, and are independent of it.
settings.content.intro: A content warning is the author's judgement about their audience, not about you. For people you read all the time, clicking through the same warning every day is friction without safety — so you can switch it off, either for everyone or for specific people.
settings.content.keptNote: Nobody is added to your list by this. Your named accounts below are kept exactly as they are, so switching back to "individual people" finds them still there.
settings.content.level.follows.note: Including people you follow in future — this is checked as you read, not copied into a list, so it keeps up on its own. Boosts are still judged by whoever originally wrote them.
settings.content.level.followsBoosts: Trust everyone I follow, and what they boost
settings.content.level.followsBoosts.note: The widest setting. A boost from someone you follow opens the warning on the boosted post too, even though you may not follow — or know — whoever wrote it.
settings.content.level.individuals.note: Only the accounts you have named, listed further down. This is the default.
settings.content.level.none.note: Every warning and blur stays in place, including for accounts on the list below.
settings.content.onServer.after: . Mawkingbird can read it but not change it — Mastodon has no API for that, so it can only be set from your server's own settings page.
settings.content.onServer.before: Your Mastodon account has its own "always expand content warnings" preference, which other apps read. It is currently
settings.content.revoke.hint: Drops to "trust no one", turns both switches off, and forgets every account you have trusted. Unlike the choices above, this one throws the list away — there is no undo.
settings.content.revokedNote: These two are off while trust is revoked. Choose another level above to use them.
settings.content.showSensitive.note: Images and video flagged sensitive render without the blur.
settings.content.title: 🙈 Trust: CW/Sensitive
settings.content.trusted.before: People whose warnings and sensitive flags are ignored, whatever the switches above are set to. Add someone from the
settings.content.trusted.empty: Nobody yet. Trusting an account is useful for someone whose posts are routinely warned but never something you need warning about.
settings.deletion.age.hint: Posts older than this many days become eligible for deletion.
settings.deletion.intro: Automatically delete your posts once they reach a specified age, with exceptions.
settings.deletion.minFavourites: Keep posts with at least this many favourites
settings.deletion.minReblogs: Keep posts with at least this many boosts
settings.deletion.title: Automatic post deletion
settings.development.intro: Applications with access to your account.
settings.development.none: No applications have been authorized for this account.
settings.development.register: New applications register themselves via POST /api/v1/apps.
settings.development.reportBug.hint: Builds a report from your description plus build and environment details. Nothing is sent automatically — you review it, then copy it or open a prefilled GitHub issue.
settings.development.title: Development
settings.filters.action.hide: Hide completely — the post disappears as if it didn't exist
settings.filters.action.warn: Hide with a warning — the post is collapsed behind the filter's title
settings.filters.edit.intro: Posts matching any keyword are hidden with a warning, or removed entirely.
settings.filters.empty: You have no filters. Add one to hide posts containing certain words or phrases.
settings.filters.intro: Hide posts containing muted words or phrases, per context. Filters apply to all sessions.
settings.filters.title: Filters
settings.filters.wholeWord.hint: Whole word: "cat" matches only the word cat, not "category". Existing keywords can be removed and re-added to change them.
settings.flags.connectors.hint.after: , greyed out. Anything you have already connected keeps its credential; it just stops being offered.
settings.flags.connectors.hint.before: One switch per service, because that is how they break — when a third-party API goes down or starts refusing browsers, turning that one off stops people setting it up and hitting the failure. A turned-off connector still appears under
settings.flags.defaultHint: Default for this release: {{default}}. It is currently {{enabled}} on this {{channel}} build.
settings.flags.intro: Choose which release channel can use features that are being rolled out.
settings.flags.overrides: Overrides are local to this browser and this published version. When the published hash changes, all flags return to the new version's defaults.
settings.flags.proxies.hint.after: . All four are off by default: each one failed often enough in testing — stripped API keys, aggressive rate limits, domain registration required, or simply very slow — that recommending them made setup look broken. What remains is the Mawkingbird proxy and any proxy you run yourself. Turning one on here adds it back to the picker, with its measured limitations written on the card. Turning one off also stops it being used if it was already selected.
settings.flags.proxies.hint.before: Which public CORS proxies are offered under
settings.flags.title: Feature flags
settings.follows.crosslink.after: does that in one pass, and tells you how many accounts it would change before you agree.
settings.follows.crosslink.before: Looking to turn retweets on or off for everyone you follow?
settings.follows.empty.anonymous: You are not following any Mastodon accounts yet.
settings.follows.intro: Pending follow requests. Requests only appear when your account requires follow approval.
settings.follows.intro.anonymous: Accounts followed by Anonymous. Sources are fetched only when you explicitly load a feed.
settings.follows.title: Approve follow requests
settings.i18n.appendTranslation.hint: Unchecked, the translation replaces the original. Checked, you get both — which is the point of learning, but costs one translation per language on a post.
settings.i18n.auto.hint.after: . Posts in a language you know are never translated, and neither are posts whose language can't be determined — those are usually English. Hovering needs a mouse, so it does nothing on a touchscreen.
settings.i18n.auto.hint.before: Translates posts in a language you're learning, using
settings.i18n.auto.hover: When I hover over a post
settings.i18n.auto.off: Off — translate only when I press 🌐
settings.i18n.auto.title: Inferred automatically
settings.i18n.auto.view: When a post scrolls into view
settings.i18n.budget.hint: Translations are counted per day and per service, and the two budgets are kept separate — running out on one never blocks the other. Counts reset at midnight, your time. Only the number of translations is stored, never what was translated.
settings.i18n.budget.total: {{count}} translated with this service in total.
settings.i18n.budget.usedUp: Today's limit is used up. Translation with this service resumes at midnight, or raise the limit below.
settings.i18n.budget.warned: Past the point where you asked to be warned. Still working, up to the limit.
settings.i18n.excludeTrends: Exclude languages I don't know from trending tags
settings.i18n.excludeTrends.hint: Hides trending hashtags that are clearly in a script for a language you haven't listed (e.g. Japanese or Arabic tags). Tags in the Latin alphabet, or ones we can't identify, are always kept. Applies everywhere trending tags appear.
settings.i18n.hideForeign: Hide posts in languages I don't know (Home and Algo)
settings.i18n.hideForeign.hint: Removes posts confidently in a language you haven't listed, or that mislabel their own language. Posts whose language can't be determined are always kept. Also toggleable with the 🌐 button on Home and Algo.
settings.i18n.intro: Tell Mockingbird which languages you read, and keep trending content relevant.
settings.i18n.known.hint: We infer these from your interface language, your browser, and your posting default. Add any others you read.
settings.i18n.learning.hint.after: by the filter above, even when it's switched on — they're the ones you're here to read.
settings.i18n.learning.hint.before: Different from the languages you know. Posts in a language you're learning are
settings.i18n.postingLang.hint: The default language Mastodon attaches to new posts.
settings.i18n.skipSame: Don't translate a post that's already in my language
settings.i18n.skipSame.hint: Skips the request when a post declares your language, or clearly reads as it — translating it would hand back the same text and still spend a call. Posts whose language can't be determined are always translated when you ask.
settings.i18n.title: Internationalization
settings.i18n.translateAll.after: foreign post, not just languages I'm learning
settings.i18n.translateAll.hint: Unbounded, and priced accordingly: every post in a language you don't read becomes a translation. Useful for reading a timeline you share no language with. Watch the daily count below.
settings.i18n.useAi: Let automatic translation spend OpenRouter credit ($$$)
settings.i18n.useAi.hint: Off by default. Choosing AI for the 🌐 button is one press you decided on; this is a loop that runs while you scroll, so it's a separate choice. Left off, automatic translation uses {{engine}} only.
settings.importExport.anon.a: You're not signed in, so anyone you follow here is saved
settings.importExport.anon.b: . They won't appear on another device, and they'll be lost if you clear your browser data.
settings.importExport.anon.c: if you want your follows kept on a server account.
settings.importExport.bridge.anon.a: Reading a server anonymously can show you public posts, but it cannot tell us who
settings.importExport.bridge.anon.b: follow — so both sides need real credentials.
settings.importExport.bridge.intro: You keep two follow lists that were built at different times. This finds the overlap: who you already follow on one network, and can now follow on the other.
settings.importExport.bridge.noMatches: No matches yet. Nobody you follow named their other account in their bio.
settings.importExport.bridge.pendingNote: didn’t name their other account. Searching for them costs one request each, so it’s opt-in and capped.
settings.importExport.bridge.signInMastodon: sign in to a Mastodon account
settings.importExport.bridge.summary.one: Read {{follows}} follows over {{pages}} page and found {{found}} from bios alone — no searches spent.
settings.importExport.bridge.summary.other: Read {{follows}} follows over {{pages}} pages and found {{found}} from bios alone — no searches spent.
settings.importExport.bridge.title: Find the same people on your other network
settings.importExport.contacts.intro: Look for the people in your contacts through your home server. Your contacts stay in this browser; only derived search terms are sent to your server. Nobody is followed automatically. Names, usernames, domains, and profile links are clues—not proof of identity.
settings.importExport.contacts.noCandidate: searched contacts had no candidate match:
settings.importExport.contacts.pickedNote: Picked from your contacts. Nothing was saved — closing this page forgets them.
settings.importExport.contacts.pickerNote: On this phone you can pick contacts directly — no export, no file. Your browser shows the picker and this page only ever sees the people you tap.
settings.importExport.contacts.skipped.a: skipped because they had no full person name or Mastodon handle. Up to

settings.rss.cache.hint: Feeds are re-read by every view that shows them. Without a cache that is a request per visit — enough to exhaust a free CORS proxy's rate limit just by reading. Cached feeds are kept in this browser's IndexedDB, which has room for feeds far too large for ordinary settings storage.
settings.rss.cors: Mockingbird has no server, so a feed only works if its site allows browser (CORS) access. Plenty don't. You'll know right away when you add one, because adding it fetches it.

settings.rss.intro: Any RSS or Atom feed becomes posts in your home feed, read-only, with an "Open original" link. No account, no credential — a feed URL is all it takes.
settings.rss.maxFeeds.hint: We suggest no more than {{recommended}}. Every feed is re-read by every view that shows them, so a long list opens slower and uses more of a free CORS proxy's quota — but it is your reading list, so set it where you want it. Lowering this never deletes a feed you already have.
